speaker_role: student (college student sharing personal Common App experience)
key_insights: Explains the Common App activities section format: up to 10 activities, 50 characters for organization/role, 150 characters for description.
Recommends using short, incomplete sentences and action verbs (oversee, lead, found, organize) to maximize limited character counts.
Advises being honest and realistic about weekly hours spent on activities, walking through a rough day/week time budget to avoid overestimating.

Recommends generally marking 'plan to continue in college' as yes for activities reflecting a genuine long-term interest, but not for narrowly local/high-school-specific ones (e.g. a local honor society).
Suggests placing smaller awards/honors related to an activity within that activity's description if they didn't make the separate 5-award list.

Recommends ordering activities by personal importance/passion (most important first) and grouping related activities together (e.g., all music or all swim activities) to show sustained thematic interest.
Advises being selective when more than 10 activities are available, prioritizing those with the greatest time commitment or role/impact.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker: Common App allows 10 activities, 50 characters for role/org, 150 characters for description
Speaker's personal example: grew Math Honor Society membership from 30 to 90 members
notable_or_distinctive: Walks through several fully worked personal examples (newspaper editor, self-started Java class for local girls, Math Honor Society, retirement-home volunteering) showing exact wording used within character limits.
reliability_notes: Personal, first-hand account from a single successfully-admitted student rather than an admissions professional; advice is generic Common App best practice with no outside sourcing; video is 6 years old so Common App character limits/format could have changed.
